1. (Original) [Claim 1 text not provided in office action; presumed to be independent claim for automated communications system]

2. (Currently amended) The automated communications system of claim 1 wherein the routing-and-message-forwarding component determines whether or not the message is authorized to be forwarded by: parsing the destination address into an ordered sequence of nodes; and for each node of the ordered sequence of nodes, determining whether the source address is authorized to send a message to that node __by accessing one or more authorization databases stored within the automated communications system__.

3. (Currently amended) The automated communications system of claim 1 wherein the routing-and-message-forwarding component determines whether or not the message is authorized to be forwarded by: parsing the destination address into an ordered sequence of nodes; and for each node of the ordered sequence of nodes, determining whether the source address is authorized to send a message to that node by __accessing one or more authorization databases to find information that authorizes the source address stored within the automated communications system, and when the source address is authorized to send a message to the node, returning an indication of success__.

4. (Currently amended) The automated communications system of claim 1 wherein the routing-and-message-forwarding component determines whether or not the message is authorized to be forwarded by: parsing the destination address into an ordered sequence of nodes; and for each node of the ordered sequence of nodes, determining whether the source address is authorized to send a message to that node by __accessing one or more authorization databases and failing to find information that blocks messages with the source address stored within the automated communications system, and when the source address is authorized to send a message to the node, returning an indication of success__.

5. (Currently amended) The automated communications system of claim 1 wherein the routing-and-message-forwarding component determines whether or not the message is authorized to be forwarded by: parsing the destination address into an ordered sequence of nodes and/or node-token pairs; and for each node and/or node-token pair of the ordered sequence of nodes and/or node-token pairs, determining whether the source address is authorized to send a message to the node by __accessing one or more authorization databases to fail to find information that blocks messages with the source address, to find information that authorizes the source address, and/or to apply any rules that apply to the message, and when the source address is not authorized to send a message to the node, returning an indication of failure, and when the source address is authorized to send a message to the node, accessing stored information within the automated communications system to determine whether or not a token associated with the node-token pair is valid, and when the token is not valid, returning an indication of failure, and when the token is valid, returning an indication of success__.
